A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Mask-GRPO work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison; v2 additionally contains a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original Mask-GRPO fine-tuning experiments, GenEval and MSCOCO-30K evaluations, ablations, and a CLIP counting analysis in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results and generated-image examples. The added checklist does not introduce further experiments.

M1.justification: The transition-probability formulations, GRPO objective, KL removal, reduction strategies, and sample filtering remain unchanged. Equation (14) is reformatted without changing its mathematical content.

E1.justification: Both versions use LAION training prompts, GenEval, MSCOCO-30K, ImageReward evaluation, and the same counting-prompt analysis. No dataset, task, or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–4 and Figure 1, including the Show-o baseline and AR-style transition-probability control. The diffusion, autoregressive, and masked-model comparison rows are retained.

E3.justification: The Show-o configuration, evaluation metrics, reduction settings, and counting-analysis procedure remain unchanged. Appendix C retains the learning rate, group size 6, and batch size 96; explicitly calling the six samples per GPU 'rollouts' clarifies the existing setting.

E4.justification: The KL, computational reduction, unmasking reduction, sample-filtering, and reward-model ablations are retained. Table 5's relative-correctness analysis and the qualitative examples also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the main scores. New checklist item 7 asserts statistical-significance reporting but points to unchanged Section 4 without adding any statistical information.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain the same numerical entries, including Mask-GRPO's GenEval score of 0.73 and MSCOCO-30K FID of 8.32. The training curves, qualitative comparisons, and Appendix D image gallery are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and reasoning are retained. Appendix B.3.1 replaces a duplicate corruption-process equation with a reference to its existing definition in B.1; Equation (14)'s line break and the ELBO equation's relocation do not alter the theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty, methodological, and performance claims: introducing GRPO to masked generative models, redefining transition probabilities, and improving generation through the same enhancements.

C2.justification: Appendix A.2 removes the causal explanation attributing autoregressive high-resolution bottlenecks to growing numbers of VQ-VAE tokens. Interpretations of CLIP rewards, KL sensitivity, and the proposed method's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C clarifies that the six samples per GPU are rollouts. Checklist item 13 newly states that all models will be released upon acceptance, adding a release commitment without establishing an actual release. Hardware, hyperparameters, and the existing code link are retained.

R1.justification: The same 87 references and research positioning are retained. Appendix A.2's shortened explanation preserves citation [79] and does not change the claimed gap concerning RL for masked generative models.

P1.justification: v2 edits affiliation and contact information, makes localized wording changes in Appendices A–C, and appends a NeurIPS checklist. The main narrative and existing section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Equation (14) is split across lines, Table 1 shifts downward, and the Appendix B ELBO equation moves onto the preceding page. The checklist adds a new layout block, while all five figures and five tables are retained.

improvement.justification: The scientific contribution and evidence remain unchanged, with modest clarification in Appendix C. However, the added checklist introduces unsupported assurances: item 7 claims statistical-significance reporting in Section 4, and item 11 claims safeguards described in Section 5, although those sections provide neither. These new inconsistencies modestly reduce reporting reliability despite the small editorial benefits.
